macro: Middle East tensions dominate: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until the U.S. meets interim deal conditions, oil hit a three-week high, and the UAE imposed a financial embargo after detecting missiles it says were launched from Iran, with Trump saying no talks are planned. Meanwhile, surging U.S. government bond yields — the 30-year hitting a 19-year high — pressured equities and drove a sharp tech selloff overnight. Retail earnings and ongoing Turkey-Israel-Syria friction are also in focus, leaving U.S. futures roughly flat.
internals_narrative: Defensive and energy leadership showed through as CommunicationServices (+1.3%), Pharma (+1.2%) and Energy (+1.1%) led while Materials (-1.2%) and Technology (-0.6%) lagged; chip and industrial names dominated the losers with INTC -6.6%, ETN -5.3%, CAT -4.6%, META -4.4% and AMD -4.3%, versus gainers INTU +4.4%, LLY +3.6% and ADBE +3.6%.

ticker_notes.INTC: Intel led decliners as chip names crumbled with the 30-year yield hitting a 19-year high.
ticker_notes.ETN: Eaton fell despite touting a collaboration with Trane Technologies to boost AI-data-center efficiency.
ticker_notes.META: Meta slid as it faces a high-stakes federal trial over child safety amid the broader tech and yield-driven selloff.
ticker_notes.AMD: AMD dropped alongside Nvidia and Broadcom as surging bond yields hit chip stocks, with commentary on dilution and insider sales.
ticker_notes.TXN: Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated a Neutral rating on Texas Instruments with a $340 price target.
ticker_notes.NEM: Newmont pulled back even as gold miners eye their best month since April 2020.
ticker_notes.NOC: Northrop Grumman in focus as Elizabeth Warren targets defense contractors' $100 billion shareholder payouts.
ticker_notes.ABBV: Wells Fargo maintained Overweight on AbbVie and raised its price target to $300.
ticker_notes.AEP: Carl Icahn trimmed his AEP stake, and Truist maintained Buy while lowering its price target to $139.
ticker_notes.AIG: Cantor Fitzgerald kept an Overweight rating on AIG but lowered its price target to $90.
ticker_notes.LLY: Eli Lilly Canada said it continues acting against unapproved retatrutide products and disputes the Canada Revenue Agency's characterizations.
